findings.source_quote: μήτιγε τὸ δοκοῦν κακῶς γίνεσθαι εὐφραίνει μὲν τὸν ποιοῦντα, κολάζει δὲ τὸν πάσχοντα;
findings.english_quote: Does not what seems to be done evilly bring delight to the doer but punishment to the sufferer?
findings.issue: “Does not” frames the question as expecting agreement. That is contextually defensible within Simon’s argument, but μήτιγε ordinarily carries a doubtful or negative expectation. Unlike the other difficult constructions here, this consequential choice of rhetorical force is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining why the argument supports the affirmative-leaning English question and preserving the doubtful alternative, such as “Is it really the case that what seems to be done evilly delights the doer but punishes the sufferer?” Alternatively, propose a less leading main question with that explanation. The revised wording or note requires fresh review; no Greek emendation or print verification is needed.

findings.source_quote: καὶ γὰρ τὸ φονευθῆναι κακόν ἐστι, κἂν μὴ πάντες λέγωσιν ὅτι μηδεὶς αὐτοπαθεῖν θέλει
findings.english_quote: For being murdered is evil, even if not everyone says that no one wants to experience it himself
findings.issue: The draft takes ὅτι as introducing the content of λέγωσιν. This is grammatically defensible, but a material contextual alternative takes ὅτι causally: being murdered is evil, even if not everyone says so, because nobody wants to undergo it himself. The alternatives change whether unwillingness to suffer murder is Peter’s asserted justification or the content of a statement not universally made. The draft does not disclose this attachment decision.
findings.suggested_revision: If retaining the main text, add a source-quoted note identifying the content-clause attachment, explaining its basis in λέγωσιν ὅτι, and preserving the causal alternative. Another candidate for fresh review is: “For being murdered is evil, even if not everyone says so, because no one wants to undergo it himself,” accompanied by the current reading as an alternative. This is a disclosure revision, not an unresolved-source block.
